title: Reconnect a pop-up stopper under a wall-hung basin: rod through the stopper, pivot nut on snug, stopper open
instruction: Push the pivot rod through the stopper's hole into the drain port, thread the pivot nut on until snug, press the rod down so the stopper lifts open, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: A bathroom pop-up stopper is lifted by a pivot rod that enters the drain from behind through a side port, passes through a hole in the stopper's shaft and is held in the port by a pivot nut, hand-tightened over a washer on the rod's ball. After the stopper has been pulled out to clear hair, or a seal replaced, the rod has to go back through the stopper's hole and the nut back on: one hand holds the rod in, the other starts the plastic nut square on its thread (crooked, it cross-threads) and turns it on until snug, then the rod is pressed down so the stopper opens. General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00, about 1.5 million in the US, BLS OEWS) and plumbers (O*NET 47-2152.00, about 0.48 million) do this under basins every day, mostly by feel and by what they can see under the basin.
setup: Station bench; positions in m from the midpoint between the arm bases (+x away from the arms, +y left, z up from the bench). One fixed layout (object_jitter 0); nothing depends on the seed. Both arms at ready. A Duravit ME by Starck wall-hung washbasin (EU 233555AA00, US 2335550000; 550 x 440 x 180 mm, bowl 520 x 290 mm) hangs low on the wall at x 0.735 (front edge x 0.295), its underside 246 mm over the bench at the drain. Its 1-1/4 in pop-up drain body (31.8 mm bore, 54 mm flange) stands at (0.455, 0.000) with its pivot port facing back (+x), 155 mm over the bench; the port thread (25 x 1.6 mm, estimate) has its first full crest marked. A Dearborn P9701 1-1/4 in plastic P-trap hangs under the drain, its J-bend swung 20 deg left and its arm cut to 17 cm. A Danco 11041 stopper (holes 1 to 5 taped over) sits closed in the drain with its 6th hole facing the port. A Danco 88532 ball rod with a 22 x 14 x 16 mm clevis connector 68 mm behind its 18.3 mm ball lies in the port's mouth, the ball 10 mm out of its seat and the tip on the seat ring; its plastic pivot nut (31 mm across the knurl, 16 mm long, a washer of 4 rubber beads facing the ball) hangs on the rod behind the ball, as in start_top.png.
scoring: Threaded: the nut counts as threaded only if its thread caught at a square start: its front face set on the port's first thread (at most 0.4 mm onto the washer), coaxial within 0.5 mm and square within 1.5 deg; a nut started crooked does not catch; turned back 3 deg past the start it comes off and can start again once 3 mm off the port. Whole-trial 0 if the rod's ball or the nut drops below 30 mm over the bench (trial video). At the end: 1.0 if the rod is in the port through the stopper's hole (ball within 3 mm of its seat, tip 3 mm or more past the stopper's middle), the nut is threaded on snug (within 20 deg of where its thread stops: turned on by hand until it stops), and the stopper is lifted 8 to 22 mm over the flange (150 mm rule; within 4 mm of the drain's axis, within 8 deg of upright) for 1.0 s with at most 2 mm drift, both hands at least 30 mm clear of the stopper, rod, nut and drain, and the stopper, rod and nut still (under 25 mm/s; trial video). 0.5 if the rod is in the port through the stopper's hole and the nut is threaded on snug, short of 1.0. 0.25 if the rod is in the port through the stopper's hole, the nut not snug. 0 otherwise.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz): the reference run reaches 1.0 at 59.9 s; the rest is room for a learned policy
reset_notes: Turn the pivot nut off the port and slide it back along the rod against the ball; pull the rod back 10 mm so its ball rests in the port's mouth with the tip on the seat ring; drop the stopper closed on the flange with its hole facing the port (check through the drain with a light); the nut hangs on the rod behind the ball as in start_top.png. About 1 minute; nothing is used up.
fidelity: Thread: the last turn before snug on a hidden carrier (a slide, three hinges; set_joint and push move only it, never the nut), welded to the nut where it stands once set square on the start (0.5 mm, 1.5 deg); 0.03 N m running torque, stop one turn on, off 3 deg back. Washer: 4 rubber beads on the ball, contact only: 4.3 N in all at snug (read in the simulator), 0.072 N m to the stop, lighter than a real hand-tightened nut. The port's lead and first crest pass the nut. No water or clevis strap.
